newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan cautions against over-regulating markets.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan cautions against over-regulating markets.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan on Friday cautioned against over-regulating financial markets but said the Fed's ability to intercept potential systemic risks should not be impeded.
In remarks to a financial markets conference sponsored by the Atlanta Fed, Greenspan said the Central Bank over the years has been able head off risks to the system before they broke out.

"Much of the types of supervision, umbrella supervision and the like, that we employ to contain systemic risk is very valuable and I would be very chagrined to see some of those powers disappear," he said, adding: "I say that from someone who believes that the less you interfere in the market, the better."
Congress is considering bank reform laws that might diminish the the Fed's authority over financial markets.
